plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid half of your value. This is because bidding higher risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing the item to someone who values it more. In this case, my value is $31, so half of that is $15.50. This strategy aims to win only when my valuation exceeds others' enough to justify the cost.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win reliably without overpaying, I'll bid slightly above this. However, my value is only 6, so I need to be very conservative. Bidding just above the expected second highest bid is too risky given my low value. A bid of 6.1 ensures I only win if another bidder drastically overestimates their value.

Given my value is $0, the optimal strategy is to bid $0. Since my value is zero, any winning bid will result in a loss equal to the second-highest bid. Bidding $0 avoids this loss. Rational bidders understand this and will not bid higher than their value. If others bid higher, I lose nothing.
